first.rationale: Activation and onboarding completion are both down 4-6% QoQ, signaling a broader engagement problem. However, the immediate competitive threat is price-sensitive SMB churn. Memory_73 shows promotional pricing was effective for that exact segment with acquisition and revenue lift plus faster time-to-first-value. Memory_31 shows that simplification alone improved activation but doesn't address price competition. A targeted promotional pricing intervention on price-sensitive SMB segments directly defends revenue while we preserve the option to debug activation/onboarding issues in parallel. This is lower-risk than attempting onboarding simplification (which requires product changes) or enterprise sales assist (which doesn't address the SMB competitive loss). Verifying memory_31 and memory_73 will confirm whether their prior lift was durable and segment-specific before committing budget.
